_comment: Validated-code dictionary for the Cg recipe library. Every entry compiles + simulates + synthesizes (yosys). kind=primitive -> general/customer-reusable; kind=example -> illustrative composition (one domain). Merge examples/*.cg into the kit; fold this metadata into _RECIPE_META.

entries.name: Recip
entries.use_when: 1/d reciprocal of a runtime value (no hardware divider)
entries.adapt: change numerator scaling; widen for more fractional bits
entries.note: bit-serial long division (digit recurrence); literal shifts only; unrolled combinational

entries.name: Divide
entries.use_when: general a/b division of runtime operands
entries.adapt: swap the numerator pre-shift for the output Q-format
entries.note: generalizes Recip; same digit-recurrence

entries.name: SeqDiv
entries.use_when: area-cheap divider when latency is acceptable (one stage reused over N cycles)
entries.adapt: change bit count / Q-format; same FSM
entries.note: rate-changing port I/O (read-when-idle, write-when-done); ~7x smaller than combinational Divide, ~48x latency

entries.name: FixedSqrt
entries.use_when: Q16.16 square root
entries.adapt: feed your value as x; keep the literal-shift isqrt loop

entries.name: RSqrt
entries.use_when: 1/sqrt(x) (normalization, inverse magnitude)
entries.adapt: isqrt then bit-serial reciprocal; both literal-shift

entries.name: SqrDist
entries.use_when: weighted squared-difference reduction with REAL input ports (datapath survives synthesis)
entries.adapt: per-element op (weights via fxmul(w,fxmul(d,d))); keep in-push ports + driver

entries.name: DotProduct
entries.use_when: fixed-point multiply-accumulate over vectors
entries.adapt: change per-element op via fxmul; add input vectors

entries.name: Fir
entries.use_when: streaming FIR filter; sample shift-register is state
entries.adapt: change taps/coeffs and tap count
entries.note: stateful streaming (one sample in/out per cycle)

entries.name: Integ
entries.use_when: Euler integrator v+=a*dt; x+=v*dt; stateful pos/vel time loop
entries.adapt: change the update rule / add leapfrog half-steps

entries.name: Distance
entries.use_when: Euclidean distance r = sqrt(sum (a-b)^2) (pre-composed MAC + isqrt)
entries.adapt: change per-term op or vector length; keep the isqrt

entries.name: Counter
entries.use_when: sequential state -> a registered output that advances each cycle
entries.adapt: change the update rule in loop(); widen the type for bigger ranges
entries.note: registered-output phase: first value out is the reset value

entries.name: BarrelShift
entries.use_when: shift by a RUNTIME amount (Cg cannot emit a variable shift) — a mux tree of literal shifts
entries.adapt: drop the arms you don't need; widen the value/amount; SRA uses i32, SLL/SRL stay u32
entries.note: the canonical workaround for 'shift by a variable' — how barrel shifters are built in RTL (literal power-of-two shifts gated by each shift-amount bit)

entries.name: RegisterFile
entries.use_when: an array addressed by a runtime index, with a hardwired-zero entry and write-first reads
entries.adapt: change entry count/width; drop the x0 guard if no hardwired zero; add or remove read ports
entries.note: runtime-indexed read AND write; entry 0 hardwired to 0 via guards (no real cell); write applied before reads

entries.name: BitFieldDecode
entries.use_when: extract a bit field from a word and sign-extend it (shift+mask, reassemble scattered bits, cast through a narrow signed type)
entries.adapt: change field positions/widths; a U-type-style upper-field needs no sign extension
entries.note: sign-extend by casting through i<N> of the field's natural width, then up to i32 (the sign bit replicates)

entries.name: Tee2
entries.use_when: replicate ONE push stream to two consumers when the branches must diverge (different rates, a transform on one side, or explicit replication in the netlist)
entries.adapt: add y2/y3... output ports for more consumers; one Tee per fan-out point
entries.note: explicit 1->2 replicator. NOT needed for plain fan-out: a bare push output wired to two consumers is a correct back-pressured broadcast (re-verified S166 in four shapes on both backends; the earlier 'fan-out deadlocks' note was wrong and cited a memory that does not exist)

entries.name: Clamp
entries.use_when: saturate/clip a value to a [lo,hi] range (overflow guard, range limit)
entries.adapt: fix lo/hi as constants for a one-sided limiter; widen the type as needed

entries.name: Lerp
entries.use_when: linear interpolation y = a + (b-a)*t, Q16.16, t in [0,1] (blend/ramp/crossfade)
entries.adapt: clamp t to [0,1] first; run one per channel to interpolate vectors

entries.name: FifoPipe
entries.use_when: buffer/decouple a producer and consumer with an elastic queue (one clock domain)
entries.adapt: change {size,width}; for two clock domains use std.fifo.AsynchronousFIFO with a clocks property
entries.note: std.fifo.SynchronousFIFO: `new ...({size,width})`; wire `fifo.reads(producer.dout)` + `consumer.reads(fifo.dout)`. Both ports are `stream` so the handshake auto-stalls (write blocks when full, read blocks when empty); the FIFO holds each element until read. Verified on BOTH bytecode and iverilog.

entries.name: MulStream
entries.use_when: stream two runtime operands through the std.math.Multiply built-in for a registered full-width signed product
entries.adapt: change the operand/product widths (product is 2x the operand width); swap std.math.Multiply for std.math.Divide for a runtime divider
entries.note: std.math.Multiply built-in: a registered (1-cycle) full-width signed product, DSP-mapped. The feeder/sink tasks bridge the network's external `push` ports onto the built-in's `stream` (valid+ready) handshake, so the multiplier's back-pressure paces the source automatically. A single task that wrote both operands and read the product would DROP a vector (the built-in is registered with no input FIFO). Verified: bytecode sim 4/4 + yosys REAL.

entries.name: ScaleGen
entries.use_when: parameterize a task by compile-time const(s) and instantiate it with new Foo({param}) — a distinct specialized module per parameter set, no runtime cost
entries.adapt: change the const params and the {..} override at the instantiation site; add more const params; widths propagate through expressions
entries.note: Generics in C⏚ = `const` params on a task + `new Scale({k: 5, w: 16})` monomorphization. Each distinct {..} makes a separate specialized module (here `Scale`), baked in at elaboration — no runtime mux or cost. Use `uint<W>` (not `u<W>`) for a parameterized width; the output width `2*w` propagates automatically. Verified: bytecode sim + yosys REAL.

entries.name: StreamDot
entries.use_when: stream a reduction (dot product / MAC / running sum) that consumes M inputs per group and emits one result; read every input stream unconditionally each cycle and gate only the emit with a counter
entries.adapt: change M (the group length) and the accumulator width; drop the multiply for a plain grouped sum; for a per-group scalar (bias) read it every cycle and use it only at cnt==0 (never read a stream inside an if); operands may be signed or unsigned (signed inline a*b of stream inputs works on the current toolchain; on releases <= 2.9.0 keep them unsigned or use std.math.Multiply)
entries.note: Streaming reduction, emit-once-per-group. Both input streams are read on EVERY cycle; the accumulator is flushed and cleared on the last element of each group (cnt==M-1). A per-group side input read conditionally (e.g. a bias read only at cnt==0) works when it is a stream (its ready/valid handshake paces it); a push input read conditionally drops the skipped values (no back-pressure). Reading every cycle is the simplest shape and works for both. Operands may be signed or unsigned (this example uses unsigned for portability; a signed inline multiply of stream inputs works on the current toolchain, and on releases <= 2.9.0 needs unsigned or std.math.Multiply). Verified: bytecode sim 2/2 + yosys REAL (47 cells) + iverilog elaborates.

entries.name: Seq1011
entries.use_when: a control FSM: an explicit enum state register + next-state logic in loop() (sequence/pattern detector, protocol controller, serial parser)
entries.adapt: change the state set and the transition table; publish outputs for the CURRENT state BEFORE transitioning; keep the enum internal and expose an integer code on the port; add input streams for a wider datapath
entries.note: The canonical control-FSM shape. State is an ENUM (named, self-documenting); this example exposes it as an integer `scode` (u2), the simplest shape for a debug signal — but an enum is ALSO a valid port type (`out St scode` carries the enum's 2-bit width directly), and a bundle-shared enum lets both sides of a cross-actor link name it. Two timing rules the compiler enforces: (1) a port reflects the register at the START of the cycle, so publish the current state and drive every output BEFORE the transition (writing a just-computed next state reads back one cycle late); (2) inline-initialize state (`St st;` defaults to the first member) instead of a setup() body — a setup() compiles to a separate reset STATE that eats the first clock and offsets the whole stream. `found` is a Mealy output (current state AND the incoming bit); `scode` is Moore (current state). Verified: bytecode sim 8/8 + yosys REAL (18 cells: adff/adffe state regs, eq compares, mux next-state tree) + iverilog elaborates.

entries.name: UartTx
entries.use_when: serialize a byte onto a one-bit line, one bit per clock (UART TX, or any start/data/stop framed serial output)
entries.adapt: change the frame width/order (add parity, 2 stop bits, MSB-first); gate the loop body behind a baud-tick enable for a real line rate; widen `data` for more bits
entries.note: A control FSM whose state is a shift register (`frame`, a u10) + a bit counter (`cnt`) rather than a named enum — the right shape when the state is just 'how many bits are left'. Idle line high; on `send` the byte is framed start(0)+8 data LSB-first+stop(1) and shifted out a bit per clock, `busy` high while in flight. Same two timing rules as any Cg FSM: publish the CURRENT line bit and busy BEFORE updating `frame` (a just-computed next bit reads back a cycle late); inline-init the registers (no setup(), which adds a reset state that offsets the stream). Write the line straight from the bit-select (`tx.write(frame[0])`) — for a bool port, write the bit itself, do not compare it (`frame[0] == 1`). One bit = one clock; gate the body behind a baud-tick enable for a real baud rate. Pair it with `UartRx` to get a full link. Verified: bytecode sim 12/12 (frame for 0x53) + yosys REAL (16 coarse cells; 49 cells / 16 FFs after full `synth -flatten` — the 10-bit frame + 4-bit counter + registered outputs) + iverilog elaborates.

entries.name: UartRx
entries.use_when: deserialize a one-bit line back into a byte (UART RX, or any start/data/stop framed serial input)
entries.adapt: change the frame width/order (parity, 2 stop bits, MSB-first); add an `out bool err` on the bad-stop branch; drive the machine from a 16x oversample tick instead of every clock for a real asynchronous line
entries.note: The exact pair to UartTx, and the deserialize half of the serial family. A falling edge (start bit) arms it, 8 cycles shift in LSB-first, the 10th cycle carries the stop bit; `valid` pulses ONE cycle when a frame is accepted. State is a shift register + bit counter, not a named enum. TWO things to get right: (1) FRAMING — the byte is committed only if the stop bit is HIGH, so a bad frame is shifted in then dropped (`data` keeps its old value, `valid` never fires); hang an `out bool err` off that else-branch to report it. (2) `data` HOLDS the last ACCEPTED byte between frames, so ALWAYS qualify it with `valid` — reading `data` on an arbitrary cycle gives a stale byte. One bit = one clock here so it pairs cycle-for-cycle with UartTx; a real asynchronous line needs 16x oversampling and mid-bit sampling, which you get by advancing this same FSM from a sample tick instead of every clock. Same two Cg FSM timing rules: publish CURRENT outputs before the transition; inline-init (no setup()). Verified: bytecode sim 24 vectors / 72 checks — accepts 0x53 AND rejects a frame with a corrupted stop bit (busy rises for it, but `data` never becomes 0x41) + yosys REAL (30 coarse cells; 62 cells / 32 FFs after full `synth -flatten`) + iverilog elaborates.

entries.name: Crc8
entries.use_when: a CRC / checksum over a serial bit stream, or the XOR-feedback shift register behind any LFSR, scrambler or pseudo-random generator
entries.adapt: change POLY and the width of `rem`/`crc` together (CRC-16-CCITT: u16 + 0x1021; CRC-32: u32 + 0x04C11DB7); init 0xFF for CRC-8/CDMA2000; drop `din` to get a plain LFSR/PRNG; unroll the body 8x over a byte for a byte-parallel CRC (the compiler flattens it to one XOR tree per output bit)
entries.note: The XOR-feedback shift register, one bit per clock, MSB-first: the top bit of the remainder XORed with the incoming bit forms the feedback, the remainder shifts left, and POLY is XORed back in when the feedback is 1. Defaults are CRC-8/ATM (poly 0x07, init 0x00). `init` clears for a new message; `en` GATES the machine so the remainder HOLDS between bursts (drive it from a link's data-valid strobe — e.g. UartRx's `valid`). THE KEY PROPERTY: feed a message then feed the CRC it produced, and the remainder returns to 0 — so a receiver never compares checksums, it just runs message AND trailing CRC through this block and checks `crc == 0`. Note `bool ^ bool` on a bit-select (`rem[7] ^ b`) is legal Cg and is the idiomatic way to write the feedback. Verified against TWO independent oracles (bit-serial model and GF(2) polynomial long division, both giving CRC-8(0x53) = 0xBE): bytecode sim 20 vectors — 0x53 -> 0xBE, HOLDS 0xBE across an en=0 gap, then feeding 0xBE back gives residue 0x00 + yosys REAL (13 coarse cells; 33 cells / 17 FFs after full `synth -flatten`) + iverilog elaborates.

entries.name: Debounce
entries.use_when: clean up a noisy/asynchronous real-world input (button, switch, sensor, off-chip level) and turn changes into one-cycle rising/falling pulses
entries.adapt: N is in CLOCK CYCLES — a 10 ms filter at 100 MHz is N = 1_000_000, so widen `cnt` to match; set N=1 and it degenerates to a plain edge detector (the classic one-cycle delay register); gate the body behind a slow tick to count milliseconds instead of cycles; drop `stable` and keep `rise` for a clean one-shot 'button pressed' event
entries.note: The canonical input-conditioning block — put it between ANY asynchronous real-world input and the rest of the design, or an FSM will see thousands of cycles of contact chatter as dozens of spurious events. State is a counter of how long the input has DISAGREED with the accepted level: disagreement counts up, agreement resets it to zero, reaching N flips the level and emits a ONE-CYCLE `rise`/`fall` pulse. A glitch shorter than N therefore leaves no trace at all. This IS also the edge detector — debounce is just edge detection with hysteresis, so N=1 gives you the plain one-cycle-delay version. Same two Cg FSM timing rules: publish CURRENT level and pulses before the transition; inline-init (no setup()). Verified: bytecode sim 26 vectors / 78 checks — a 3-cycle glitch against N=4 is REJECTED outright (`stable` never moves), a sustained change is accepted after exactly N cycles, and there is exactly ONE rise and ONE fall pulse in the whole trace + yosys REAL (21 coarse cells; 34 cells / 11 FFs after full `synth -flatten`) + iverilog elaborates.

entries.name: Pwm
entries.use_when: generate a duty-cycled output (LED/motor/DAC/servo) OR divide a fast clock down to a slow one-cycle tick that gates another machine
entries.adapt: PERIOD is in CLOCK CYCLES — widen `cnt` to hold it (868 needs u10, 100_000 needs u17); drop duty/pwm/dreg for a pure clock divider; count up-then-down for centre-aligned PWM; instantiate per channel with new Pwm({PERIOD: n})
entries.note: Counter + compare — the two things you build from a free-running counter. `pwm` is high for the first `duty` of every PERIOD cycles; `tick` is a one-cycle wrap pulse. THE `tick` IS THE RATE DIVIDER the UartTx/UartRx notes point at when they say 'gate the loop body behind a baud-tick enable': at 100 MHz a 115200-baud UART needs a bit every 868 cycles, so PERIOD=868 and wire `tick` to the UART's enable — the UART FSM is unchanged. THE PART PEOPLE GET WRONG: `duty` is LATCHED into `dreg` at the period boundary, not compared live; using the live input lets a mid-period change cut a pulse short and emit a runt cycle that shows up as flicker. Both outputs are pure Moore precisely because of that latch. Verified: bytecode sim 24 vectors / 48 checks — `duty` is deliberately changed MID-period and the period in flight is proven undisturbed (period 2 keeps duty 3, period 3 picks up 6), tick lands exactly every PERIOD + yosys REAL (13 coarse cells; 41 cells / 12 FFs after full `synth -flatten`) + iverilog elaborates.

entries.name: SpiMaster
entries.use_when: drive an SPI bus as master (ADC, DAC, flash, sensor, display controller) — clock out a byte and clock one in at the same time
entries.adapt: invert `sclk` for mode 3 (CPOL=1), swap which half samples/shifts for the CPHA=1 modes; widen sh/rsh/tx/rx and `cnt` for 16- or 24-bit frames; hold `csn` low across several bytes for multi-byte flash/display transactions; one `csn` per slave sharing sclk/mosi/miso; gate the body behind a Pwm `tick` for a slower sclk
entries.note: The clock-GENERATING side of a synchronous serial bus, and the counterpart to the UART pair. SPI is FULL DUPLEX: one byte goes out on MOSI while another comes back on MISO in the same eight bit-times — there is no separate read transaction, which is why one `start` pulse carries both `tx` and `rx`. Unlike a UART the master owns the clock, so there is no baud agreement and no start/stop framing; `csn` frames the transfer instead. One SPI bit = TWO fabric clocks via the `ph` phase register: ph=0 sclk LOW (MOSI stable for the slave), ph=1 sclk HIGH (slave sampled MOSI on the rising edge, master samples MISO here, MOSI advances on the fall) — that is mode 0. `rx` HOLDS the last byte, so qualify it with `done`, same rule as UartRx's data/valid. sclk is fabric/2 here (the fastest possible); gate the body behind a Pwm tick to slow it. Verified: bytecode sim 21 vectors / 105 checks of a real full-duplex exchange — MOSI carries 0x53 MSB-first while 0xA5 is simultaneously clocked in, csn is low for exactly the 16 transfer cycles and high outside, one `done` pulse + yosys REAL (48 coarse cells; 84 cells / 43 FFs after full `synth -flatten`) + iverilog elaborates.

entries.name: Accumulator
entries.use_when: add each input to a running total held in a register and output it
entries.adapt: widen the accumulator for longer runs; subtract the leaving sample for a moving sum; accumulate a*b for a MAC; clamp before the write to saturate
entries.note: One register updated every cycle. The out sync write lands in the SAME cycle as the read, so publishing AFTER the update includes this cycle's input; swapping the two lines gives a one-cycle lag, which is the usual off-by-one here. The accumulator is wider than the input by design. yosys_cells measured with the documented coarse flow.

entries.name: Lfsr
entries.use_when: generate a pseudo-random bit or word per cycle — PRBS test patterns, scrambling/descrambling a serial link, dithering, randomised backoff, or a cheap substitute for a binary counter
entries.adapt: change the width of `st`/`prbs`, the bit index in `st[7]` and LFSR_POLY together (primitive low-words: u8 0x1D, u16 0x2D, u24 0x87, u32 0xC5) and update the period assert to 2^n - 1; feed a data bit into the feedback (`fb = st[7] ^ din`) and it becomes Crc8; XOR `dout` with a payload for a scrambler (the receiver must seed identically — that is what a link preamble is for)
entries.note: The Galois form: shift left, and XOR the polynomial back in when the bit shifted OUT is 1 — one XOR per bit rather than the Fibonacci form's feedback tree, so it runs faster for the same sequence. MAXIMAL LENGTH is the property that matters and it is CHECKED BY RUNNING IT: the companion `Lfsr_test` network free-runs the register and asserts the seed returns after exactly 255 cycles (2^8 - 1) while the state never visits 0. A wrong tap set fails loudly — 0x1B gives period 51, and the mutation test confirms both the vector fixture and the period assert fire. THE ONE FAILURE MODE: all-zero is a fixed point, so the seed must be non-zero; the monitor asserts against it every cycle. NOT a cryptographic RNG — n output bits reveal the state by linear algebra. `en` gates the register so the sequence survives gaps, `reseed` restarts it. Shows a FILE-SCOPE `const` (declared after the package and before the first entity) shared between the task and the test network's monitor. Verified: bytecode sim 24 vectors / 48 checks + the 255-cycle period network + iverilog VALUE sim 48/48 identical + ghdl analyses the VHDL clean + yosys REAL (12 coarse cells; 32 cells / 17 FFs after full `synth -flatten`), no inferred latches.

entries.name: PriorityEncoder
entries.use_when: turn a request/bit vector into the INDEX of the first set bit plus a valid flag — interrupt controllers, free-list allocators, cache-way selection, float normalisers, and the encode step inside any arbiter
entries.adapt: reverse the if/else chain for MSB-first (highest bit wins = floor(log2)); output `W-1 - idx` for a leading-zero count; widen `req` and `idx` one `else if` per bit, and past ~8 bits split the word into groups, encode each, encode the group-valid vector with a second copy, and concatenate the two indices; add a rotating priority pointer and it becomes RoundRobinArbiter
entries.note: Pure combinational: no state, no clock behaviour, and the ORDER OF THE if/else CHAIN IS THE PRIORITY (lowest bit wins here). THE `valid` FLAG IS NOT OPTIONAL — index 0 is both a legal answer and the natural nothing-set default, so `idx` alone cannot tell 'requester 0 is asking' from 'nobody is asking'; a consumer that forgets to qualify it grants an idle bus to requester 0 forever. Same data/valid discipline as UartRx's byte. The fixture pins the priority rather than the popcount: 0x03 -> 0, 0x06 -> 1, 0xFF -> 0, 0xF0 -> 4. Mutation-tested by reordering the chain (bit 1 first), which the fixture catches. Verified: bytecode sim 16 vectors / 32 checks + iverilog VALUE sim 32/32 identical + ghdl analyses the VHDL clean + yosys REAL (22 coarse cells; 32 cells after full `synth -flatten`), no inferred latches.

entries.name: RoundRobinArbiter
entries.use_when: hand a shared resource (bus, memory port, output link, DSP tile) to one of N requesters per cycle without starving anyone — the fair alternative to a fixed-priority encoder
entries.adapt: widen req/grant/base/sel and add rotate cases + encoder branches for more requesters (past ~8, rotate a GROUP vector and use the two-level encoder from PriorityEncoder); gate the grant and the pointer update on a `done`/`last` input for multi-cycle burst ownership; add per-requester credit counters that mask `req` for weighted round-robin; replace the single pointer with an ordering register for LRU; delete `base` and the rotate to fall back to fixed priority
entries.note: ROTATE, ENCODE, ROTATE BACK — the standard construction that turns fair arbitration (hard) into fixed priority (an if/else chain). Rotate `req` right by the pointer so the requester with top priority lands in bit 0, run an ordinary lowest-bit-first encode (literally PriorityEncoder, narrowed), add the pointer back to get the real winner, then move the pointer to winner+1 so the winner now has the LOWEST priority. That last line IS the fairness invariant. There is no barrel shifter in Cg (see BarrelShift), so the rotate and the one-hot `1 << sel` are muxes over literal shifts — at N=4 that is the entire cost of fairness. FAIRNESS IS CHECKED EXPLICITLY, not just 'someone got granted': with all four requesting for eight straight cycles the grants are 0,1,2,3,0,1,2,3 — each requester served exactly twice, never twice in a row, where a fixed-priority arbiter would print requester 0 eight times. The fixture also pins that the pointer SKIPS silent requesters (req=0b1010 alternates 1,3,1,3 rather than wasting turns), HOLDS while nobody asks (no drift), and does not force a hand-off when only one requester wants the bus. Mutation-tested by disabling the pointer update — the fixture fails immediately. Verified: bytecode sim 19 vectors / 57 checks + iverilog VALUE sim 57/57 identical + ghdl analyses the VHDL clean + yosys REAL (38 coarse cells, 21 muxes + 2 adders; 53 cells / 10 FFs after full `synth -flatten`), no inferred latches.

entries.name: GrayCounter
entries.use_when: count in a code where only ONE bit changes per step — a pointer that has to be sampled by another clock domain (async FIFO), an absolute position/shaft encoder, or a low-toggle-rate bus; also the reference for the binary<->Gray conversions themselves
entries.adapt: widen everything together — the decode needs one XOR term per bit (u8: >>1..>>7, or a two-stage prefix tree), and a Gray counter is only single-bit-change if its length is a power of two (a mod-10 Gray sequence must be hand-built); take `gray` through `std.lib.SynchronizerFF` per bit and decode in the far domain for a CDC pointer; keep only the decode half for a position encoder
entries.note: Counts in BINARY and derives Gray — the right way round, because the Gray->binary decode is an XOR PREFIX (W-1 logic levels) and you do not want it on every use. The two conversions are one line each: `g = b ^ (b>>1)` and `b = g ^ (g>>1) ^ (g>>2) ^ (g>>3)`; the fixture checks the ROUND TRIP by requiring `decoded == bin` on every cycle. THE DEFINING PROPERTY IS CHECKED IN HARDWARE: `onestep` compares this cycle's Gray word with last cycle's and asserts the difference is a single bit, via the power-of-two test `d != 0 && (d & (d-1)) == 0`. The fixture pins it high on every cycle following an increment INCLUDING the 15 -> 0 wrap (Gray 8 -> 0), which is the case a naive implementation gets wrong, and low while `en` is low because no step happened — it is a check on increments, not a property of the wire. WHY IT MATTERS: a binary 7 -> 8 sampled by an unrelated clock can read as 15 or 0, values the counter never held; with Gray only one bit is ever in flight so the worst case is the old value or the new one. That is the async-FIFO pointer rule, and this project shipped a VHDL AsynchronousFIFO that crossed BINARY pointers for exactly this reason — prefer `std.fifo.AsynchronousFIFO`, which now Gray-codes them. Mutation-tested with `b ^ (b>>2)`, caught by the fixture. Verified: bytecode sim 21 vectors / 84 checks + iverilog VALUE sim 84/84 identical + ghdl analyses the VHDL clean + yosys REAL (23 coarse cells; 51 cells / 17 FFs after full `synth -flatten`), no inferred latches.

entries.name: EdgeDetect
entries.use_when: turn a LEVEL into a one-cycle EVENT — every 'start' strobe, every 'this just changed', every level-to-pulse conversion; the smallest and most-instantiated block in a design
entries.adapt: compare a WIDE value (`din != prev` on a u8/u32) for a 'value changed' / register-write strobe; take `both` after a 2-flop synchroniser for the classic toggle-to-pulse CDC handshake; latch `rise` into a sticky bool cleared by the consumer for an interrupt-status bit; initialize `prev` to your signal's idle level if a cycle-0 edge is wrong for you
entries.note: ONE delay register and three gates: rise = din & ~prev, fall = ~din & prev, both = din ^ prev, and every strobe is exactly one cycle wide however long the level is held afterwards. That is the point — an FSM waiting on a level re-triggers forever; an FSM waiting on `rise` triggers once. The strobes are MEALY (same cycle as the transition, no added latency); `dly` exposes the register itself for aligning a datapath. TWO PRECONDITIONS, both in the header: (1) SYNCHRONISE FIRST — an off-chip or cross-domain input needs `std.lib.SynchronizerFF` in front or metastability becomes a phantom edge; (2) DEBOUNCE IF IT BOUNCES — a mechanical contact produces hundreds of real edges and this block faithfully reports all of them, so use `Debounce` (which is this block plus a hysteresis counter) and take ITS rise/fall. Rule of thumb: clean logic signal -> EdgeDetect, anything touched by a human or a wire -> Debounce. NAMING TRAP recorded in the source: the third output is `both`, not `edge`, because `edge` is a Verilog keyword — Cg accepts it and emits the escaped identifier `\edge ` while its companion `edge_valid` is NOT escaped, which is legal but unpleasant to wire up. Mutation-tested (rise = d || !prev), caught by the fixture. Verified: bytecode sim 16 vectors / 64 checks — 4 rises, 4 falls, 8 both, including a 1-cycle blip and back-to-back edges + iverilog VALUE sim 64/64 identical + ghdl analyses the VHDL clean + yosys REAL (12 coarse cells; 9 cells / 6 FFs after full `synth -flatten`), no inferred latches.

entries.name: Biquad
entries.use_when: a second-order IIR filter section in fixed point — low/high/band-pass, notch, shelf, peaking EQ, DC blocker or PLL loop filter; cascade several for higher order
entries.adapt: recompute b0,b1,b2,a1,a2 (RBJ cookbook / scipy butter, iirnotch, ...), multiply by 2^QS and round — nothing else changes; a DC blocker is b=[1,-1,0], a=[1,-0.995,0]; instantiate once per section and chain them for higher order (cascade in increasing Q); clamp the output instead of letting it wrap (see Clamp) — an IIR that wraps can enter a permanent limit cycle; raise QS with the coefficient and accumulator widths for a closer match to the designed response; add `(1 << (QS-1))` before the shift to round instead of truncate
entries.note: Direct Form I: y[n] = b0*x[n] + b1*x[n-1] + b2*x[n-2] - a1*y[n-1] - a2*y[n-2]. Five multiplies, four adds, four registers, one wide accumulator and NO intermediate rounding. Q FORMAT IS STATED EXPLICITLY, because leaving it implicit is how a day disappears: coefficients are Q2.14 signed (value * 2^14; range [-2, 2), the tightest format that always holds a stable biquad's a1), samples are plain integers but may be any consistent Qm.n since the filter is linear, and the i32 accumulator is sized from max|x|*(|b0|+|b1|+|b2|) + max|y|*(|a1|+|a2|) ~ 8e8. THE THREE TRAPS, all documented in the source: (1) `>> 14` FLOORS, it does not round, and the feedback path recirculates the bias — which is why the step response settles at 997 not 1000, and the fixture deliberately pins the truncating behaviour because that is the hardware; (2) the FEEDBACK MUST USE THE TRUNCATED output, not the wide accumulator, or you have built a different filter than the one you simulate; (3) DF-I over DF-II in hardware — the two extra registers are free and DF-II's internal state has a dynamic range unrelated to the signal's. Coefficients are an RBJ Butterworth low-pass at fc = fs/8, Q = 0.7071. The fixture is the STEP RESPONSE (rise, ~5% overshoot to 1054, settle, decay, then a negative step for the sign path), generated by an integer Python model of exactly this arithmetic and cross-checked against a float reference (max deviation 2.3 LSB, all truncation bias). Mutation-tested by moving ONE coefficient by ONE LSB (B1 3199 -> 3200) — the fixture catches it. Verified: bytecode sim 28 vectors / 28 checks + iverilog VALUE sim 28/28 identical (so the signed multiplies and the arithmetic right shift survive the Verilog backend, cf. the signedness traps in feedback_compiler) + ghdl analyses the VHDL clean + yosys REAL with all FIVE $mul cells present (15 coarse cells; 3291 cells / 65 FFs after full `synth -flatten`, i.e. the multipliers are genuinely there and would map to DSP tiles).

entries.name: Manchester
entries.use_when: send data down one wire with no separate clock — a self-clocking, DC-balanced line code with an encoder/decoder pair (10BASE-T, RFID/NFC, IR remotes, DALI)
entries.adapt: invert `line` (and the recovered bit) for Manchester II / G.E. Thomas polarity; encode by presence/absence of a transition at the START of the bit for DIFFERENTIAL Manchester (immune to a swapped pair); gate both blocks behind one Pwm `tick` at twice the bit rate for a real line rate; add a preamble generator and a preamble detector (a shift register + compare, see Seq1011) for framing; the same skeleton with different transition rules gives BIPHASE MARK / FM0 (S/PDIF, AES3)
entries.note: An encoder AND a decoder, each with its own vector fixture, PLUS a `Manchester_test` network that wires them back to back and asserts the ROUND TRIP — 0xB2 in, 0xB2 out. bit 1 -> low then high, bit 0 -> high then low (IEEE 802.3; the opposite of G.E. Thomas / Manchester II, and the two are endlessly confused — say which you mean). WHAT IT BUYS: a transition in the middle of EVERY bit, so clock recovery always has something to lock to, and exactly half of every bit-time is high, so DC balance is exact and data-independent and the link can be transformer- or capacitor-coupled. WHAT IT COSTS: two line transitions per data bit — half the payload rate of NRZ, which is why gigabit links scramble (see Lfsr) instead. THE THIRD PROPERTY, and it is not an afterthought: the code is SELF-CHECKING. High or low for a whole bit-time is not a legal symbol, so `viol` reports a missing mid-bit transition — 10BASE-T transmits exactly such an illegal symbol as its end-of-frame delimiter. Both blocks run at TWO CLOCKS PER BIT off one phase register, so the encoder expects `din` HELD for the whole bit-time (which is what a real source does). DELIBERATELY OMITTED: phase acquisition — these two start in phase because they start together; a real receiver oversamples 4x-16x or locks to a preamble (that is what Ethernet's 1010... is for). Mutation-tested twice — inverting the encoder polarity and making the decoder take the FIRST half-bit — both caught. Verified: bytecode sim ManchesterEnc 16 vectors / 32 checks + ManchesterDec 24 vectors / 72 checks (including two deliberate coding violations and recovery afterwards) + the round-trip network + iverilog VALUE sim 32/32 and 72/72 identical + ghdl analyses the VHDL clean + yosys REAL (11 + 18 coarse cells; 9 cells / 5 FFs and 15 cells / 9 FFs after full `synth -flatten`), no inferred latches.

entries.name: HammingEcc
entries.use_when: correct a single-bit error and DETECT a double-bit error in a stored or transmitted word — ECC memory, NAND controllers, registers that must survive a single-event upset, and links too slow to retransmit
entries.adapt: scale to the (72,64) DRAM/cache standard with 8 parity bits (7 Hamming + 1 overall) over 64 data bits — generate the 64-input XOR trees from the position masks rather than writing them out; drop the correction mux for detect-only (much smaller, and right when you can retransmit); drop the overall parity for SEC-only ONLY if a double error is genuinely impossible, or you have built a machine that confidently corrupts data; INTERLEAVE several codewords, or use Reed-Solomon, for burst errors; use Crc8/CRC-32 for pure detection over a long message
entries.note: Extended Hamming(7,4) = (8,4) SECDED, with the encoder, the decoder AND an ERROR-INJECTION port in one block, so the entire claim is testable in a plain vector fixture: `code` is the clean codeword, `err` is a bit mask XORed into it (the channel), and dout/corrected/dblerr are what the decoder makes of the damage. THE CONSTRUCTION, worth understanding rather than memorising: parity bits sit at the POWER-OF-TWO positions and each covers the positions whose index has its bit set (p1: 1,3,5,7 · p2: 2,3,6,7 · p4: 4,5,6,7), so recomputing the three parities over the received word and reading the results as a binary number gives THE POSITION of the flipped bit directly — no table, no search. Plain Hamming(7,4) has distance 3 and silently 'corrects' a double error to the wrong data; the overall parity p8 lifts it to distance 4 and separates the four cases (parity fails + syndrome != 0 -> one error at `syn`; parity fails + syndrome 0 -> the error is in p8 itself; parity holds + syndrome != 0 -> TWO errors, detected not correctable; both clean -> clean). THE DED HALF IS THE WHOLE VALUE: it turns a silent wrong answer into a loud one. `dout` IS MEANINGLESS WHEN `dblerr` IS HIGH and the fixture shows it (vector 18 asks for 0xB and gets 0xE) — that is what 'detect but do not correct' means. `1 << syn` would be a variable shift, so the correction is a mux over eight literal masks (see BarrelShift). Also demonstrates the bool-packing idiom: `(u8) someBool` is a TYPE ERROR in Cg, so bits are packed with `(b ? 1 : 0) << k`. The Python oracle was checked EXHAUSTIVELY first — all 16 data words x (1 clean + 8 single-bit + 28 double-bit patterns) = 592 cases — and the 22 shipped vectors are its readable subset, covering every one of the 8 single-bit positions (including a hit on p8 itself, syndrome 0, which a naive decoder mishandles) and 7 different double-bit errors. Mutation-tested by dropping one term from p2. Verified: bytecode sim 22 vectors / 88 checks + iverilog VALUE sim 88/88 identical + ghdl analyses the VHDL clean + yosys REAL (119 coarse cells: 36 $xor for the parity trees + 43 $mux for the correction; 99 cells after full `synth -flatten`), no inferred latches.

entries.name: MovingAverage
entries.use_when: smooth a stream by averaging the last N samples — an ADC reading, a sensor, a packet-rate estimate, or an error signal in front of a control loop
entries.adapt: change N with the array size and the width of `wp` (u3 addresses 8, u4 addresses 16) and keep `acc` wide enough for N*max(x); make x/win/acc signed for signed samples; swap the array for `std.mem.SinglePortRAM` for a large window so it maps to block RAM; use Fir instead when you want a shaped response (a moving average has a poor sinc-shaped stopband and is chosen for its price); use `acc = acc - (acc >> k) + x` (see Accumulator) for an EXPONENTIAL moving average with no buffer and no warm-up
entries.note: THE TRICK IS THE RUNNING SUM: the window only changes by one sample per cycle, so `acc = acc - (the sample leaving) + (the new one)` is one add and one subtract regardless of N — O(1) arithmetic with O(N) storage, in a circular buffer indexed by a wrapping write pointer (a runtime array index, as in RegisterFile). This block is Accumulator plus a subtraction. READ `win[wp]` BEFORE WRITING IT — `wp` points at the oldest sample AND at the slot the newest goes into, so the wrong line order subtracts the sample you just wrote and the sum drifts forever; the mutation test drops the subtraction entirely and the fixture catches it. `full` IS NOT DECORATION: the buffer starts zero-filled, so for the first N-1 cycles the average is diluted by samples that never existed (the fixture shows the output ramping 1, 3, 7, 12 while the input is already 10, 20, 30, 40) — ignore `avg` until `full`, or preload every slot with the first sample. DIVIDING BY N COSTS NOTHING AND N NEED NOT BE A POWER OF TWO: the compiler folds `acc / 8` to a shift and `acc / 10` or `acc / 3` to a single-cycle reciprocal multiply, so pick the window your signal wants; only a RUNTIME divisor needs std.math.Divide. `acc` must hold N*max(x) or it wraps. The fixture drives a lone 200 into a stream of 80s and pins both halves of the smoothing: the average moves by 20 rather than 120, and vector 19 is the moment the spike slides OUT of the window again (95 -> 80). Verified: bytecode sim 23 vectors / 69 checks + iverilog VALUE sim 69/69 identical + ghdl analyses the VHDL clean + yosys REAL (65 coarse cells: $add/$sub plus the 8-deep register window; 413 cells / 89 FFs after full `synth -flatten`), no inferred latches.
